standard.title: Guidelines for Fixing Intensity of Irrigation (सिंचाई की तीव्रता निश्चित करने के मार्गदर्शी सिद्धांत)

sectional_committee.name: River Valley Projects: Planning, Irrigation Management and Evaluation Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies standard guidelines, parameters, and socio-economic or hydrological criteria for determining and fixing the intensity of irrigation in river valley projects, differentiating between intensive and protective irrigation systems to optimize water allocation, maintain smallholder viability, and promote sustainable agriculture.
standard.scope: This standard specifies standard guidelines, parameters, and socio-economic or hydrological criteria for determining and fixing the intensity of irrigation in river valley projects, differentiating between intensive and protective irrigation systems to optimize water allocation, maintain smallholder viability, and promote sustainable agriculture.

certification.description: Voluntary Guidelines. Since IS 13668:1993 is a planning guideline and methodology standard rather than a physical consumer material, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its planning criteria, water duty computations, and commanded-area calculations is strictly mandated by the Central Water Commission (CWC), state irrigation and water resources departments, and agricultural ministries during the preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), feasibility briefs, and funding clearances for major and medium river valley projects across India.
requirements: Formally defines the intensity of irrigation as the percentage of the culturable commanded area (CCA) proposed to be irrigated in a given period of time, such as a crop season or a full water year.

For intensive irrigation systems (where water availability is not a limiting factor), the intensity of irrigation may be set to 100 percent or even more. This objective is met by putting the same land under multiple cropping cycles once or twice a year under different crops.

For protective irrigation systems (where water is scarce), the primary objective is to extend irrigation facilities to a larger, more dispersed area. Consequently, the design intensity is set low to distribute benefits across the community, provided the lower limit is fixed to maintain the basic viability of small agricultural landholdings.

Fixing high intensities in water-sufficient zones is shown to support better utilization of agricultural inputs (like fertilizers and modern implements) and take advantage of residual soil moisture from previous crops.

Fixing a suitable intensity requires careful evaluation of several factors, with water availability serving as the primary physical constraint. Where water is abundant, high intensities are called for, while water-scarce zones must adopt protective, lower-intensity limits.
